title: Self-host your everyday apps
intro: Photos, passwords, films, notes and PDFs on a machine you own. Each of these runs in Docker on a spare computer or a small server, and stands in for a service you'd otherwise rent.
repos: immich-app/immich
Phone photo backup and a gallery with search, in place of Google Photos
dani-garcia/vaultwarden
A password server that works with the Bitwarden apps and fits on the smallest machine
jellyfin/jellyfin
Streams your own films and music to any device, with no account and no fees
usememos/memos
Quick notes on a personal timeline, in place of Google Keep
Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF
Merge, split, sign and convert PDFs without uploading them anywhere
home-assistant/core
Runs the house: lights, sensors and automations that keep working offline
louislam/uptime-kuma
Watches all of the above and tells you when one goes down

title: Replace your team's SaaS stack
intro: The tools a small team pays for every month, each with an open source project that does the same job. Start with the one whose bill annoys you most.
repos: makeplane/plane
Issues, sprints and docs, in place of Jira or Linear
penpot/penpot
Design and prototyping in the browser, in place of Figma
nocodb/nocodb
A spreadsheet face on a real database, in place of Airtable
twentyhq/twenty
A CRM you can shape to your own sales process, in place of Salesforce
go-gitea/gitea
Git hosting with code review and CI on your own server
apache/superset
Dashboards and charts over your data, in place of Tableau
supabase/supabase
Database, auth and storage for your app, in place of Firebase

title: Run AI on your own machine
intro: From working out what your hardware can run to chatting with a model that never leaves it. In roughly the order you'd need them.
repos: AlexsJones/llmfit
Start here: tells you which models fit your memory and GPU
open-webui/open-webui
The chat window for local models, with history, files and users
lyogavin/airllm
Fits large models into a small GPU by loading one layer at a time
jundot/omlx
A fast model server made for Apple Silicon Macs
unslothai/unsloth
Fine-tune a model on your own data without a data centre
vllm-project/vllm
When one machine becomes a service: high-throughput serving
jamiepine/voicebox
Voice cloning, dictation and speech, all generated locally

title: A better terminal
intro: Seven upgrades that make the command line faster and friendlier. None needs the others, so take them one at a time.
repos: ghostty-org/ghostty
A fast terminal that feels native on each platform
starship/starship
A prompt that shows what matters (branch, runtime, status) in any shell
atuinsh/atuin
Searchable shell history, synced across your machines
BurntSushi/ripgrep
Search a codebase in milliseconds, skipping what git ignores
nushell/nushell
A shell where command output is tables you can filter and sort
tldr-pages/tldr
Man pages cut down to the five examples you actually wanted
schollz/croc
Send a file to another computer with one command and a code phrase

title: Build with MCP
intro: MCP is how AI agents reach outside tools. These are the servers worth plugging in first and the kit for writing your own.
repos: modelcontextprotocol/servers
The reference servers: read these to see how one is put together
PrefectHQ/fastmcp
The quickest way to write your own server, in Python
github/github-mcp-server
Gives an agent your issues, pull requests and repos
ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
Lets a coding agent open a page and read the console and network
upstash/context7
Feeds agents current library docs so they stop inventing APIs
punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers
The directory to browse once you want more

title: Notes that live on your device
intro: Note apps that keep your writing in files on your own machine first, with sync as an option and no lock-in.
repos: logseq/logseq
An outliner that links every note into a graph, stored as plain Markdown
siyuan-note/siyuan
Block-based notes with databases, and sync you can host yourself
fastrepl/anarlog
Records and summarises meetings on your own computer
colanode/colanode
Team chat and a shared knowledge base that work offline
ZhFahim/anchor
A simple offline-first notes app you can self-host
memex-lab/memex
A phone journal that organises entries for you
